uncited: **Inputs:** A sequence of regular Cartesian grids representing a time series.
**Outputs:** A BSAMR structure comprising nested LODs per time step, SFC indices for each brick, and a Brick for Brick Addressing Table (BFAT).
**Brick:** A group of voxels treated as a single loadable unit.
**LOD (Level of Detail):** A grid resolution level.
LOD0 is the coarsest, covering the entire domain.
**BFAT (Brick for Brick Addressing Table):** A 2D sparse matrix.
*   **Y-axis:** Temporal dimension (time steps).
*   **X-axis:** LOD information, ordered from coarsest (left) to finest (right).
The matrix is sparse because AMR hierarchy varies; early time steps may have fewer refined LODs or different cardinalities.
**Pre-processing (Conversion):** Convert the input sequence of regular Cartesian grids into a sequence of BSAMR structures.
**SFC Indexing:** Apply a Space-Filling Curve (SFC) method, specifically the Hilbert curve, to index each AMR brick uniquely.
**Storage:** Store individual scalar values of each brick in individual binary files.
*   **SFC Order:** The order of the Hilbert curve can be adjusted per LOD.
*   **Brick Size:** The number of voxels per brick.
*   **Hierarchy Variation:** The AMR hierarchy may vary across time steps, leading to a sparse BFAT where some LODs may not exist or have different cardinalities in early time steps.
*   **Nested Order:** The nested order must be strictly respected.
LOD0 always covers the entirety of the domain, ensuring no empty space.
Uses tetrahedral elements instead of voxel bricks.
Chosen when unstructured mesh topology is required. [1094-tet-amr-data-structure.md]
Focuses on precise ray-element intersection for AMR data.
Chosen when geometric accuracy is critical over performance. [4399-exact-amr-rendering.md]
Applies filters to reconstruct scalar values from AMR data.
Chosen when smoothing or anti-aliasing is needed. [5581-amr-basis-reconstruction-filter.md]
*   **Time Complexity:** Pre-processing involves SFC indexing, which is $O(N \log N)$ for $N$ bricks due to sorting.
Storage and retrieval are $O(1)$ with BFAT lookup.
*   **Memory Complexity:** The BFAT is a 2D sparse matrix, storing only valid indices.
Memory usage scales with the number of bricks and LODs.
Performance depends on the efficiency of the Hilbert curve implementation and I/O throughput.

*   **When Not to Use:** When unstructured mesh topology is required (use TET-AMR) or when exact geometric intersection is critical (use Exact AMR Rendering). [1094-tet-amr-data-structure.md][4399-exact-amr-rendering.md]
BSAMR was introduced in the context of GPU-based out-of-core architecture for interactive volume visualization of AMR time series.
The method leverages Block-Structured AMR and Space-Filling Curves to enable efficient data access and rendering.
